title: Xbox Game Pass Gets Even More Games In November
description: The second half of November is usually quiet for several reasons when it comes to new game releases–and one other big reason–but Xbox Game Pass subscribers can look forward to several new titles to close off the month. Microsoft has announced a handful of new additions to the Game Pass library, including a kid-friendly game to kick things off and a sneak peek at some sporty fun for the first week of December. These announcements typically come in two waves, with a sneak peek split between them, so this list isn't complete yet. As soon as the rest of the lineup is announced, we’ll update this post with a closer look at what you can download and play soon. The first game on the way is Paw Patrol: Dino World. Ideal for younger members of the family who definitely shouldn't be playing GTA 6 right now, this family-friendly game revolves around the PAW Patrol working together to round up lost and scared dinosaurs. Starting in December, you can get Freestyle Football 2, which is an online multiplayer soccer game built around 5v5 matches. We already have that game in the form of Rematch from Sifu developer Sloclap, but if you want a different spin on that soccer idea, take a quick look. Xbox Game Pass November Wave 2 Games November 17 Paw Patrol: Dino World (Xbox Series X|S, PC) December 3 Freestyle Football 2 (Xbox Series X|S, PC) November has been pretty good for new entries in the Game Pass library, with the start of the month bringing the dungeon-crawling roguelike deck-building game Dungeon Crawlers to more Game Pass tiers, while subscribers also got Void/Breaker, Warhammer Survivors, and John Carpenter’s Toxic Commando. Game Pass Essential saw a big influx of new games, with several Banjo-Kazooie titles joining People Can Fly’s Gears of War prequel and the beloved Viva Piñata games.

title: We Got A Grand Theft At Disney World Before GTA 6
description: The "We got X before GTA 6" meme continues as a Grand Theft has been reported at Walt Disney World's Epcot theme park just days before Rockstar's open-world crime game releases, and the meme comes to an end. The Walt Disney World: Active Calls account, which tracks police reports in the Disney World area, said a Grand Theft call at Epcot came in at 9:52 PM on November 14. There are no further details to go on here, but Grand Theft, known as Grand Larceny in some states, involves stealing something valuable. Epcot and Disney in general has lots of items that would be considered valuable. This is the closest that Disney World might come to GTA 6, as Rockstar already confirmed that GTA 6 won't have its own version of the park. That makes sense, too, considering Walt Disney World is located in Orlando and GTA 6 takes place in its own version of Miami, which is more than 200 miles away. Calls for Grand Theft are not uncommon at Disney World. In October 2026 alone, the County Sheriff's Office received at least seven Grand Theft calls. One of the most infamous heists at Walt Disney World took place at Epcot. In 2018, thieves nabbed the multi-hundred-pound Buzzy animatronic from the Cranium Command attraction, which was housed at Epcot's shuttered Wonders of Life pavilion. It has never been recovered. A documentary, Stolen Kingdom, was released in 2025, chronicling the heist and the wider black market for Disney props. More recently, the Paddlefish restaurant at the Disney World entertainment district, Disney Springs, was robbed by someone who swam up to the waterside restaurant in frogman gear, forced two workers into a corner, obscured the security camera with foam, and made off with cash. This case has not been solved. In other Disney news, the entertainment giant is teasing "major" announcements for The Game Awards next month. As for GTA 6, the game finally releases on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. The "We got X before GTA 6" memes have been among the most…

title: GTA 6 Promo At KFC Is A Fake Funeral So You Can Take The Day Off To Play
description: The popular fried chicken chain KFC has announced a frankly absurd GTA 6 promotion: a fake funeral so people have a “legitimate” excuse to take the day off to play Rockstar’s latest. The fake funeral for a woman, "Ann Alibi," will take place Thursday, November 19 at 11 AM at KFC Robina in Queensland. People can attend in person or watch the funeral by livestream. The local restaurant is part of a region of Australia known as the Gold Coast, which KFC says is the equivalent of GTA 6's Vice City (which itself is a stand-in for Miami). RIP "The service will include a hearse, coffin, floral tributes, a book of condolences, an order of service and even a heartfelt eulogy delivered by a surprise guest. All the appropriate arrangements for a fitting farewell," KFC said. The restaurant is also handing out free fried chicken to anyone who shows up in person. For those who can't make the services, KFC will offer free delivery through its app across Australia on November 19. Anyone planning to eat fried food and play video games should be mindful of what might happen to their controller... unless you got your hands on the limited-edition "greaseproof" controller that Microsoft put out years ago. Check out the video below to see how an Xbox controller holds up to heavy grease. A KFC spokesperson said of the GTA 6 promo, "We appreciate that Australians have responsibilities, but some occasions are simply too important to miss. And in accordance with Ann's final wishes, we've made sure the funeral takes place during working hours." GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. People in Australia will be among the first in the world to play it since the game unlocks at midnight local time and not simultaneously around the world. This means people in the US will be among the last in the world to get to play GTA 6.

title: Xbox Is Looking For Smarter Ways To Stop Its Next Console From Costing A Fortune
description: No one knows yet exactly what the next-gen Xbox console, Project Helix, will be, but most people are convinced it won't be cheap. The ongoing memory shortage has driven current-gen console prices skyward since 2024, with the Xbox Series X rising from $500 in 2020 to $800 in 2026. Project Helix is projected to cost as much as $1,800 at launch, but Microsoft aims to keep the price down when it eventually releases the device. According to VP of next-gen Jason Ronald, techniques like neural rendering could help manage costs. "It's definitely a challenging time, but as a system and a platform designer, it's also one of the most exciting times, because we have to invent entirely new technology to continue to advance the state-of-the-art while also continuing to make things accessible and affordable," Ronald said in the Xbox 25th Anniversary Magazine. "This is a big reason why we're really focused on advancements like neural rendering, because it's an entirely new way to generate a frame without requiring more computational horsepower, additional memory, and things like that. I think you're going to see more innovation over the next three to five years than you've seen in the last 10 years." In a nutshell, neural rendering uses AI to predict and generate high-quality video game frames while using only a portion of hardware power, similar to upscaling technoligies like PSSR, DLSS, and FSR. This could enable next-generation visual leaps while keeping the console accessible and reasonably priced for consumers. The other benefit is that the AI software models can improve over time through updates, as console hardware remains fixed over its lifespan, hence Ronald's quote about improvements reaching Project Helix over a few years into its run. It remains to be seen how these breakthroughs will be spread across Project Helix, which Ronald teased as a family of devices that can address home, mobile, and cloud gaming needs. title: Xbox Project Helix Is A Console That Plays PC Games, Not The Other Way Around
description: Xbox has revealed more details about its next-gen device, Project Helix, describing it as a "console capable of playing games from your PC." Prominently featured in the Xbox 25th Anniversary Magazine, VP of next-gen Jason Ronald said the Xbox Series X|S successor is designed to build on the successes — and hard lessons — of previous Xbox generations, with fewer barriers to play. "When we think about Project Helix, it's really designed to be the ultimate gaming machine--one that removes all the barriers of play that have historically existed," Ronald said. "My entire library is accessible to me. I'm able to bring four generations of my Xbox library and progression with me and have it available instantly. And we remove the arbitrary constraints between console and PC games." Ronald added that the Project Helix family of devices isn't purely focused on traditional next-gen themes like better graphics, but on thinking ahead to create "innovative" experiences. "We don't think the next generation is defined by 8K, or 240 hertz, or some of the traditional metrics--it's really about gameplay innovation," Ronald explained. "We're very clear on the design goal: Helix is designed to be a console that is also capable of playing games from your PC. It is not a PC that can also play console games. The goal is making it easy, intuitive, and instant to access my games. But if you're a hardcore gamer or a power user who wants to have that deeper level of customizability across settings and performance options, you can absolutely go do it." Project Helix will also let "hardcore" gamers customize their gaming experience, but how much will all of this cost? Xbox isn't revealing a ballpark figure for Project Helix yet, but Ronald did mention the company is aiming to balance state-of-the-art gaming with an "affordable" price tag. title: All Hail Blood Gulch, Halo’s Greatest Multiplayer Map
description: After 25 years, Halo can be remembered for many things. It's among the best launch games of all time, which was pivotal in making Xbox a serious console contender. Its campaign was so brilliantly designed, from set pieces like The Silent Cartographer to the distinct and believable AI behaviors, that it was one of the few games at the time that compelled me to replay on its hardest difficulty. But perhaps what has made it so meaningful and memorable over the years--which is sadly absent from the recent Halo: Campaign Evolved--is its competitive multiplayer. And I can't really think about Halo multiplayer without thinking of Blood Gulch, especially when it was essentially the only map I would ever play with friends. Multiplayer sessions fixated on just one map was a bit of a common occurrence among my friends, given the countless sleepovers that involved GoldenEye on the N64 and doing nothing but having shootouts in the toilets of Facility. In comparison, Halo took a while to make an imprint for us, considering that I had to wait until the following Christmas after its launch before I could get an Xbox. I was also the only person among my friends to own Microsoft's console, but Halo's influence would spread like The Flood when I introduced it to my friend Josh. We had gone to different schools in sixth form but stayed in touch as I was going to church back then, so it became a ritual that after evening service, he would come around to my place to work through Halo's campaign in co-op. By the end of its explosive final mission, he was converted and got his own Xbox. Halo: Combat Evolved - Blood Gulch It was also at this point where we were able to meaningfully experience Halo's multiplayer. After all, shooting at each other in 1v1 matches was a bit one-note, but Josh also had younger brothers, so suddenly I was going over to his house with spare controllers so we could play four-player splits-screen just like the N64 days. This was when we got our introduction to…

title: I Loved My Xbox 360s–All Four Of Them
description: Xbox is celebrating its 25-year anniversary today, November 15, 2026. Below, we take a look back at Microsoft's great, and infamously buggy, second console. In the mid to late aughts, the Xbox 360 reigned supreme. It felt like the center of the gaming universe, as the best place to play multiplatform hits like Modern Warfare and Grand Theft Auto, and the only way to play exclusive blockbusters like Halo 3. All of my high school friends were on Xbox Live every night, and online gaming became a ritual to me. My clearest, purest memories of gaming come from this era, and the Xbox 360 remains one of my favorite consoles of all time. It’s too bad that I burned through so many of them. The Xbox 360 was as infamous for hardware failures as it was famous for its amazing software library. It’s nearly impossible to look back at the 360 without also recalling the Red Ring of Death, the ominous three red lights surrounding the power button that indicates a general hardware error. This red ring was a plague on the initial Xbox 360 model, and the shipping and repairs for affected consoles cost Microsoft a little over a billion dollars. The Xbox 360 platform as a whole had an amazing lifespan--the first Xbox 360 consoles themselves, though, did not. Halo 3 Somehow, I had completely avoided the dreaded red ring with my original 360 model, but it wasn’t spared of all technical issues. One night, I plopped my Halo 3 disc in the tray, only to be met with a suspicious clicking-like noise. Instead of the Halo 3 icon appearing on my dashboard, a generic “Open Tray” message appeared in its place. Troubleshooting was a maddening process--all of my discs were returning the same message, and Google searches were largely unhelpful. Despite the functioning software, my 360 refused to read any of my physical games. It quickly became clear that my 360 was a lemon. I removed the hard drive, enveloped my 360 in bubble wrap, stuffed it in a box, and left it with UPS. The ordeal cost me $90, as my…

title: The Sunday Papers
description: While following a peculiar trail of silver and saffron leaves around the largest roots of the Treehouse, you come across a hexagonal wooden door lying half-hidden among ivy and moss. Scraping away the dirt, you discover a faint, absurd engraving of a newspaper. What mystery is here? You turn the brass knob – strange, it is warm! – and the engraving of the newspaper flutters. The pages turn faster and faster, emitting a howling gale that bowls you head over foot. When you pick yourself up, you are inside a vast attic full of books and bricabrac, lit from one side by windows that offer no view of the outside world – just light and mist. Tarnation! You have been lured into the eternal prison of Sunday Afternoon. Fortunately, there are several ways to escape. Each of the arcane objects before you is secretly a portal, transporting you to another site of arcane activity, in a bizarre web of diversions that cannot possibly reflect the hand of a human curator. Which will you choose? Read more

title: GTA 6 Is Like The Olympics – “A Rare Cultural Moment” With Massive Ripple Effects
description: After years of development, multiple delays, and what can only be assumed to be one of the biggest production budgets ever, Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 launches on November 19. The game is poised to "blot out the sun," some experts believe, and its release looms so large that other gaming companies are shifting dates for their own games to stay out of the blast radius. Francis Lawrence, the director of the new Hunger Games movie Sunrise on the Reaping, which comes out a day after GTA 6, has said he hopes people can find the time to play the game and watch his movie. In short, GTA 6 is seen by some as a black hole that will suck up time, attention, and money from the broader gaming economy--and even workplaces, as people dive into the 80-hour game they've been waiting a decade to play. To help make sense of, and contextualize, the enormity of GTA 6's looming launch, GameSpot caught up with Bart Spiegel of the global professional services and research company PricewaterhouseCoopers, or PwC. He told GameSpot that GTA 6 is "something much bigger than a traditional entertainment launch," and is more akin to an event like the Olympics. He believes GTA 6 is a "rare cultural moment" that "commands extraordinary attention and creates economic activity well beyond the event itself." Jason pumping some iron in GTA 6. Spiegel said he foresees potential shifts beyond gaming, in places like TV viewership, music consumption, social media engagement, and even travel. "In an increasingly fragmented entertainment landscape, it's rare for a single release to command this much attention across so many industries simultaneously. That's what makes this moment so significant," he said. An economics professor recently claimed that about 1.5 million people plan to "call out sick" to play GTA 6, and this could come at a "cost" of $1 billion to the US economy. Spiegel said people should remember that GTA 6 isn't anything new or special as it relates to taking time off work. "People…
